context: Squire must know the Squire owner's Claude plan and how much of it is used, pace itself, never spend beyond the plan without the owner's yes, warn and wait for a yes before a big job, give upgrade advice once, and keep long conversations going with a handover note and a timely /clear prompt (AC-1301-1, AC-1301-2, AC-1301-3, AC-1302-1, AC-501-1, AC-501-2). The big jobs themselves (research, apps, sites, video and audio) are built later and go through the gate decided here. Facts, each from its source: Claude Code names no plan tier in a documented field (commands, cli-reference and statusline pages; ADR-004 reads an undocumented subscriptionType at sign-in only to refuse a plan below Pro). The status line command, set in settings as statusLine with type command, receives JSON on stdin with model.id, context_window.used_percentage, rate_limits.five_hour.used_percentage and rate_limits.seven_day.used_percentage (0 to 100) and each window's resets_at (Unix epoch seconds); rate_limits appears only for claude.ai Pro, Max and Ultra subscribers and only after the first API response in the session, each window may be absent on its own, and a window is dropped once its resets_at passes; the command runs when a session starts or resumes, when a new assistant message arrives and after /compact, debounced at 300 ms, and its triggers can go quiet when the session is idle (statusline page, read 2026-11-15). /usage is a screen for a person; /usage-credits opens the usage-credits billing settings; /upgrade opens the upgrade page (commands and costs pages). opus, sonnet and haiku are usable on any paid plan; a Fable model can bill to usage credits instead of the plan's included limits and the model picker then marks it "Requires usage credits"; no list of models an account can use is documented (model-config page). SessionStart's source is startup, resume, clear, compact or fork, and Claude Code adds the plain-text stdout of a SessionStart or UserPromptSubmit hook to the session's context; PreCompact's trigger is manual or auto; no hook input documents a usage or rate-limit field (hooks page, read 2026-11-15). Owed: whether the status line command runs inside the kept-alive Remote Control session at all, and whether it receives rate_limits there; the probe on a test Mac planned for it was not driven on 2026-11-15 (no connection to the test Mac was open). Anything not stated by a source is marked as this record's decision.
decision:
1. The plan the owner declares. Set-up's window "Squire: your Claude plan" (ADR-004's, shown at the one yes, before the name) stays the one place the plan is asked, once per set-up, with its choices Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise, Free and I'm not sure; Free is refused there as it is today. When set-up writes the name and personality into the owner's squire.json (the step that makes the owner's folder), it writes the answer there too, as claudePlan, in the words chosen ("Pro", "Max", "Team or Enterprise" or "I'm not sure"). The plan is the owner's word, never read and never changed by Squire; a set-up run again that does not ask again keeps it.
2. The usage snapshot. core/tools/status-line.py is Claude Code's status line command in core's settings (statusLine, type command, run by /usr/bin/python3 -B from ${SQUIRE_HOME}/core as the hooks are). With the status line JSON on stdin it writes runtime/usage.json in the Squire home, whole, through a file beside it and a rename, mode 0600, holding exactly: at (seconds since 1970, when written), model (model.id), contextUsedPercent (context_window.used_percentage, or null), fiveHour and sevenDay, each {usedPercent, resetsAt} from rate_limits.five_hour and rate_limits.seven_day (resetsAt in seconds since 1970), or null when that window is absent. Nothing else: no prompt, no path, no session id, no token, no cost. It prints at most one plain line for the status display and always exits 0; input it cannot read as JSON changes nothing, so the snapshot only ages. The source: the probe on a test Mac planned for it was not driven (2026-11-15: no connection to the test Mac was open), so whether this command runs inside the kept-alive Remote Control session, and receives rate_limits there, is still owed; until a probe shows otherwise the status line command is the source, and a Stop hook is the named fallback.
3. Unknown. The snapshot is unknown when runtime/usage.json is missing, cannot be read, or its at is more than 3600 seconds before now; a window is unknown when it is null. Unknown defers nothing and asks for no second yes; every heavy job still asks (line 6), and its warning says Squire cannot see the plan's usage right now.
4. Pacing, from a known snapshot when a job comes up; every threshold is strictly above. A job that can wait is a heavy job (line 6): no other job reaches Squire's code before it starts. Five-hour window above 80%, or weekly window above 70% (the criterion's either): the job is deferred: its warning names each window over its threshold, its percentage and when it resets (HH:MM, 24-hour, the Mac's local time, with the weekday when it is not today), and says the job can wait until then; it starts only on the owner's yes, as always. Weekly window above 70%, besides: on the owner's first message of the local day the prompt hook (core/hooks/user-prompt-submit.py) adds Squire's own note, in the release note's form ("Squire note from Squire's own code (not a message from anyone): "), saying the weekly allowance is at N% and when it resets and suggesting lighter work for routine jobs; once a day, never again the same day. Above 90% in either window: line 6's second yes.
5. No spend beyond the plan. The floor (core/hooks/pre-tool-use.py) refuses, yes or no, any tool call that would turn on usage credits or open the upgrade page: /usage-credits or /upgrade run through a tool that runs slash commands (SlashCommand), or given to the claude command line; the owner does both himself, and Squire only ever names /upgrade in its advice (line 7). The floor asks before any model outside the plan's set is picked, its block naming usage credits: the plan's set is opus, sonnet and haiku (model-config page); the routes are the Agent tool's model, and a claude command line's --model, a --settings value that names a model, or ANTHROPIC_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL or CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL set for it. An Agent call that names no model, or one in the plan's set, stays free. A yes covers that one call, once. Claude Code's settings stay the floor's (no model change through them) and no key is ever set (ADR-003 line 4).
6. The heavy-job gate. A heavy job is deep research, building an app, building a site, or video and audio work. Each starts only through Squire's job command, /usr/bin/python3 '<Squire home>/core/tools/heavy-job.py' research|app|site|media, its path quoted as the health check's is. The floor asks the owner before every start, whatever the usage: the block's first line is "Request <id>: this is a big job: <deep research | building an app | building a site | video and audio work>", then the usage (each known window's percentage and reset; line 4's deferral; or, when unknown, that Squire cannot see the plan's usage right now), then the ask words every request carries. The request is recorded in the approvals ledger, its item heavy:<class>; a yes covers that one start, once, and never another class. Above 90% in either known window, once the first yes is given the floor raises a second request for the same start, its block saying usage is above 90% and a second yes is needed, and the start runs only once both are given. Allowed, the command prints one line saying the job has started on the owner's yes, and exits 0. Spelt any other way the floor cannot read as this one command (inside a shell's -c, chained with another command, or by changing folder into core), the start is refused as any program naming Squire's home is; a path through a link that resolves to this command is this command. The instruction block the session loads (Persona) tells the session to start every heavy job this way, naming the command, and to wait for the yes. The jobs' own tools, built later, run only within a job whose heavy-job yes is in the ledger (AC-1302-2).
7. Upgrade advice. The prompt hook adds Squire's own note on the owner's message once the trigger is met: three five-hour limits reached in the last 7 days, or one weekly limit reached in the last 30 days, with more than half of the messages Squire took in over that period the owner's own (a message framed "Squire wake-up:" is Squire's own background work and is not requested). A limit is reached when the status line command sees a window at 100%, counted once per window and resetsAt; the records kept for this live in runtime/ in the Squire home and hold no message text. The note says plainly that a bigger plan would help, quotes no price, changes nothing, and ends "Your call. Type /upgrade if you want to look." Given once, it is recorded in runtime/advice.json in the Squire home as {"givenAt": <seconds since 1970>}, and it is not given again for 30 days (2592000 seconds) from givenAt, whatever the owner answers: after a no, Squire stays quiet for a month. It never changes claudePlan or any setting and never opens /upgrade (line 5).
8. The handover note. When context reaches 70% (contextUsedPercent at or above 70 in a known snapshot) or after the session's second compaction (SessionStart with source compact, counted per session id), the prompt hook's note on the owner's next message asks the session to save its handover note (the work in progress, what is done, what is next, where things are) with the Write tool, as a new file, to <owner folder>/state/handover/<session id>.md, which the floor lets through without a yes; that note does not mention /clear. Once that file exists and is not empty, the prompt hook's note on the owner's next message (a natural pause: no turn in flight) asks the session to ask the owner to type /clear when ready, saying the note is saved and nothing will be lost. If the owner carries on without /clear, the prompt comes back at a later natural pause: the owner's first message after the session restarts or compacts again. At SessionStart with source clear, core/hooks/session-start.py prints the newest handover note not yet picked up, whole, after one line saying it is the handover from the last conversation, so it reaches the new conversation's context, and records it picked up in runtime/ in the Squire home; startup, resume and compact print no handover. Squire never deletes a handover note, so it survives a restart, a further compaction and a late /clear. The hooks still always exit 0.
9. Where it lives. runtime/ in the Squire home is a floor path: the session can neither write nor forge a snapshot or a record there. New entry points: core/tools/status-line.py and core/tools/heavy-job.py; changed: pre-tool-use.py, user-prompt-submit.py, session-start.py, set-up.py, Persona and core's settings. The pure rules (the thresholds, the staleness rule, the advice trigger) are module functions in core/lib, each testable alone. The ticket contract (ADR-005 lines 4 and 16 to 19) is not touched.
consequences: Usage model for the thresholds and caps; every figure is an assumption, none measured. Typical profile: a Pro owner with a few conversations a day (20 to 40 light turns) and about one heavy job a week; the five-hour window peaks at 30 to 60% and the weekly at 20 to 50%: nothing is deferred, there is no weekly line, each heavy job takes one yes and the advice never fires. Heavy profile: an owner running a deep research and an app build on the same day beside everyday chat; the five-hour window reaches 85 to 100% two or three times a week and the weekly passes 70% by mid-week: heavy jobs are deferred with the reset time, the weekly line comes once a day from then on, a heavy job above 90% takes a second yes, the advice comes once after the third five-hour limit in a week (or the first weekly limit in a month) and then stays quiet for 30 days. The hour of staleness: the status line runs on each assistant message, so a session idle for more than an hour has an unknown snapshot until its next turn, and the first heavy job after an idle hour asks with "cannot see" in place of the figures; a heavy job is never started on a stale reading. Context: a typical day reaches 70% of the context window or a second compaction every few days, one handover each time; a long build session can reach it within hours, still one handover per conversation. The plan tier is the owner's word, not read: a wrong answer changes only the words of the advice, never a gate. Field names can change between Claude Code versions: the status line command fails soft, and a snapshot it can no longer write ages into unknown, which asks more, never less. If the probe shows the status line does not run under Remote Control, the Stop hook writes the same snapshot (it needs the same proof); if neither carries the windows, every heavy job asks with usage unknown and the site's words about keeping the owner informed change (the owner's call). Squire's session gains no new approval channel: every yes is the owner's own message to the floor's request, as ADR-003 line 8 has it.

alternativesConsidered.name: The Stop hook as the snapshot's source
alternativesConsidered.summary: Write the snapshot from a Stop hook at the end of each turn.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: No hook input documents a rate-limit field (hooks page); it is the named fallback if the probe shows the status line does not run under Remote Control, and it needs the same proof.

alternativesConsidered.name: Read /usage
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: A screen for a person, not machine-readable (commands and costs pages).

alternativesConsidered.name: Read the plan tier from claude auth status
alternativesConsidered.summary: Use the subscriptionType set-up reads at sign-in as the plan.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Undocumented, so it can change without notice; the criterion asks for the plan the owner declares, which set-up already asks once.

alternativesConsidered.name: Ask the plan again beside the name, or in the first conversation
alternativesConsidered.summary: A second place to ask the plan.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Set-up already asks it once at the one yes; asking again would ask the owner twice.

alternativesConsidered.name: Gate heavy jobs by the tools they use
alternativesConsidered.summary: Treat any web search, any subagent or any long run as a heavy job.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Cannot decide the class (a light lookup uses the same tools) and would ask for every small job; one job command the floor asks for, named in what the session loads, with the jobs' own tools refusing without its yes, decides it.

alternativesConsidered.name: Ask, rather than refuse, for usage credits and the upgrade page
alternativesConsidered.summary: Let the owner's yes turn credits on or open /upgrade from the session.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Both are money the owner does himself (the design study: Squire never turns on usage credits and never opens /upgrade); failing closed, Squire refuses and names the command for the owner.

alternativesConsidered.name: Advice quiet only after a no
alternativesConsidered.summary: Give the advice again until the owner says no.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Would repeat while the owner ignores it; quiet for 30 days from the advice, whatever the answer, is once and never nags.

alternativesConsidered.name: A Mac dialog for the big-job warning
alternativesConsidered.summary: Show the warning outside the session.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: The floor's block, relayed by the session, is Squire's one approval channel (ADR-003 line 8).

title: Plan awareness and the heavy-job gate: the declared plan, the usage snapshot, pacing, no spend beyond the plan, upgrade advice once, and the handover note
